max_colour_notes: max.jpg colour policy, presentation only — no effect on any FITS or on the brightness series. max_neutral 1.0 white-balances on the linear data and stretches all three channels against ONE shared clip pair, instead of the old per-channel auto-WB stretch that broke the fixed ratio between channels. max_saturation 0.2 then scales the chroma that survives. WHY SO LOW: max.jpg is stretched very hard (lo 25 / hi ~99.5 over a near-black sky), so a single ADU of chroma noise becomes ~50 levels of colour — the vivid green/magenta was amplified noise, not sky. It cannot be balanced away, only scaled down. Chosen by Peter 2026-09-19 off a six-panel sweep on astrocam 2026-09-16 (panel F), the brief being that the bright colours are likeable but make no sense to a visitor. SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-26 position (session #332) that the false colour was deliberate — that sweep varied area_gain/sky_frac/max_hi_pct only and never put a colour axis in front of him to choose from. Paired with the nightly-cam change that stores each winning pixel's CONTRAST-NORMALISED rgb rather than its raw ADU; that is what fixed the blotchy patches and the trails chopped at the patch seams.
name: starcam
black_level_notes: OV5647 electronic zero, PER FRAME in 10-bit LSB-aligned ADU, measured from this camera's own 4x coadd floor: 61.184 / 4 = 15.30. Independently corroborated by eclipticam-v1 (10180/10/64 = 15.9). Added 2026-08-20; this camera has no `pedestal` (chart floor) because it has no live brightness chart — add one if that changes, and do NOT reuse this value for it.
blackest_observed_notes: Darkest recorded frame mean on the 4x-COADD basis (n=7116, 2026-05-24) — i.e. 4 frames summed, so ~15.30 per frame, which lands on black_level with essentially no footroom. The other starcam mode (ov5647_10bit_subs) floors at 0.001, meaning its black level was already subtracted upstream; those two modes are NOT on a common scale. Resolve before using starcam in any cross-camera accumulation.
plate_scale_notes: THEORETICAL, not plate-solved: 206.265 * 1.4 um / 300 mm = 0.9626 arcsec/px. Field of view 0.693 x 0.520 deg. Supersedes the stock-lens value 0.0206 deg/px (53.50 deg horizontal, heavy barrel distortion) - that lens is off the camera. Barrel distortion is gone; a 300 mm Newtonian is near-rectilinear across a 3.6 mm chip. REPLACE THIS from the streaks themselves: trailed stars self-calibrate, since streak length at known exposure gives plate_scale*cos(dec) and streak direction gives orientation - available on every frame, and tracks flexure/focus drift in a way a one-off plate solve does not.
pole_prior_notes: Nulled 2026-09-08. Was [910, 40] for the stock 53.5 deg lens. Meaningless behind a telescope: the celestial pole cannot be in a 0.69 x 0.52 deg field unless deliberately pointed there, and the polar-derotation/star-trail pipeline this fed does not apply.
night_layout_notes: night/YYYY-MM-DD/HH/<epoch_ms>.npy raw Bayer from the Pi 1B; to-fits converts in place to .fits.fz; HHb/ siblings hold 2x2 binned frames.
processing_host_notes: Pi 1B cannot process on-host; all pipeline stages run on puppy where the NFS frames land.
s3_legacy_notes: Dual-publish target during transition — the live /starcam/* website pages read this bucket.

optics.type: Newtonian reflector, spherical primary, tabletop alt-az Dobsonian
optics.notes: Celestron FirstScope, International Year of Astronomy 2009 edition (21024-IYA; same optics as the stock 21024, commemorative decals). Replaces the OV5647 stock lens. NO tracking and NO finder - both are operational constraints on the capture design, not footnotes.

resolution_notes: Sampling is far finer than this scope delivers. Airy disk 1.22*lambda/D = 3.6 arcsec across at 550 nm; the primary is SPHERICAL at f/3.95, giving roughly D/(2048*lambda*F^3) = 1.1 waves P-V of spherical aberration, ~4x the Rayleigh quarter-wave limit. So real star images are several arcsec wide against a 0.96 arcsec pixel. The OPTICS are the resolution limit here, not the seeing and not the sensor - which means 2x2 binning costs nothing real and buys signal and Pi-1B throughput. Prefer the binned path.

drift.notes: Alt-az, undriven, and the smear is TREATED AS SIGNAL rather than as a limit (Peter, 2026-09-08). Sidereal drift is a deterministic 1-D box convolution: direction and length are computable from geometry and exposure time and are near-uniform across a 0.69 deg field, so this is KNOWN-PSF deconvolution, not blind. Trailed stars also carry astrometry - streak length at known exposure gives plate_scale*cos(dec), streak direction gives field orientation. There is therefore NO per-sub trailing cap; an earlier version of this file asserted 0.064 s and was wrong.
drift.sub_length_rationale: In the read-noise-dominated regime total SNR at fixed integration time is INDEPENDENT of sub length (signal per streak pixel = f/k, independent of t), so sub length is chosen on practical grounds, not photometric ones. On a Pi 1B the practical grounds all favour LONGER subs: fewer frames, less I/O, less NFS traffic. Sub length only begins to cost SNR once sky shot noise catches read noise, ~14 s on assumed RN=3e-/QE=0.4 (UNMEASURED - see read_noise_todo). Working range 1-4 s = 16-64 px streaks, tractable to deconvolve.
drift.vary_sub_length: DO alternate sub exposure lengths across a stack. A box kernel's MTF is a sinc with exact nulls at n/L where information is destroyed outright; nulls for L1 do not coincide with nulls for L2, so mixed exposure lengths fill in each other's dead frequencies. Coded exposure in the time domain, for the cost of a config change.
drift.field_rotation: Alt-az: negligible within a sub (~1 arcsec at field edge over 14 s) but real across a night. Registration must solve ROTATION as well as translation, and the rotation rate diverges near the zenith.

read_noise_todo: UNMEASURED. RN~3e- and QE~0.4 are assumed, and every noise threshold above rests on them. ~7116 frames already exist (see blackest_observed); the frame-difference of two matched darks gives RN directly. Measure before tuning gain.
